issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §9 (Contains, In, After, Before, Ends, Starts, Except, Expand) — operand typing for interval-valued list selections
issues.evidence: Interval operands derived from list expressions — First({Interval[4,6]}), Last(...), collapse(...)[1], or any LIST_EXTRACT over an interval list — are not recognized as intervals by _is_fhir_interval_expression (fhir4ds/cql/translator/expressions/_temporal_intervals.py:465). Symptoms (both py and cpp engines, .temp/qa/cql15_explorer3_2026_08_21/probe3.py, probe4.py): 'First({Interval[4,6]}) contains 5' -> DuckDB string contains Binder Error; '5 in First(...)' -> Binder Error; 'First(...) after/before Interval' -> UDF TypeError int/str comparison; 'First({Interval[4,6]}) ends Interval[1,6]' -> SILENTLY WRONG False (expected true: bounds-list coercion re-wraps LIST_EXTRACT as intervalFromBounds(x,x)); same for starts; '(collapse ... per 2)[1] except Interval[4,6]' -> null instead of interval pieces; 'expand First({Interval[4,6]}) per 1' -> list of degenerate interval structs instead of points [4,5,6].
issues.root_cause: LIST_EXTRACT/list_extract over interval-producing sources is missing from the interval-expression recognition sites; the {low,high} bounds-list coercion path then misinterprets it.
issues.resolution: Extended _is_fhir_interval_expression (fhir4ds/cql/translator/expressions/_temporal_intervals.py) to recognize LIST_EXTRACT/list_extract over interval-producing sources (SQLList/SQLArray of intervalFromBounds, from_json(collapse_intervals[_per]), and direct interval-UDT calls); expand single-interval routing (_translate_expand) now honors interval-typed LIST_EXTRACT operands. Regression: test_interval_part1_parity.py::test_cql_interval_part1_explorer3_list_extract_interval_operands_route_as_intervals. Note: QA reproducer expectations for '(collapse ... per 2)[1]' were miscalibrated — collapse per 2 spec-merge yields a single Interval[1,6], so index [1] is correctly null/absent; indexer over the non-per collapse output behaves as expected.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §9 Expand: boundaries more precise than per are truncated to per precision (Interval[@T10:00,@T12:30] per hour -> {T10,T11,T12}); boundaries less precise than per contribute nothing for Date/Time (Interval[@T10,@T10] per minute -> {})
issues.evidence: expand Interval[@2024-01-01T10:30, @2024-01-01T12:00] per hour -> ['2024-01-01T10','2024-01-01T11'] on both engines (missing T12; boundaries not truncated to hour precision). expand Interval[@2024-01, @2024-01] per day -> ['2024-01-01'] (spec: no contribution -> {}). Numeric case expand Interval[1.2,3.0] per 1 -> [1.2,2.2] matches the DBCG Java reference engine (grid from start, no numeric low truncation) though it diverges from spec prose. .temp/qa/cql15_explorer3_2026_08_21/probe5.py
issues.root_cause: Python _expand_temporal and _expand_time plus the C++ ExpandTemporalInterval did not truncate more-precise temporal boundaries to per precision, and Date/DateTime boundaries coarser than per contributed a point instead of nothing.
issues.resolution: Truncate-to-per-precision plus no-contribution rule for coarser boundaries implemented in fhir4ds/cql/duckdb/udf/interval.py (_expand_temporal via _raw_dt_rank/_truncate_dt_to_rank, _expand_time via millis floor to per unit) and extensions/cql/src/cql_extension.cpp (ExpandTemporalInterval truncate lambda, ExpandTimeInterval unit_ms floor); C++ binary rebuilt + md5-deployed. Numeric grid behavior (DBCG Java reference: expand Interval[1.2,3.0] per 1 -> [1.2,2.2]) preserved. Regression: test_interval_part1_parity.py::test_cql_interval_part1_explorer3_expand_temporal_boundary_truncation.
